Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for England's reply with the bat! The umpires walk out to the middle. And it has gotten pleasingly bright and sunny out there. Now then, New Zealand Women Under-19 players form a team huddle before scattering around the park. Out walk the English opening pair of Davina Perrin and Jemima Spence. And it will be Louisa Kotkamp to kickoff the proceedings with the new ball for New Zealand. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, with 90 runs to chase, the momentum firmly is in England's favor. The English batters would aim at replicating their bowling dominance and chase this down without losing too many wickets. However, the in-form Kiwi bowling attack won't go down without a fight. It will be interesting to see how the English openers negotiate the first six overs. An exciting run-chase is up next, folks!

Kate Irwin is up for a flash interview. She says that hitting the gaps worked for her today and she was looking to run hard and get to a good start. She further talks about being positive at the top working for her well in this tournament. Ends by saying that the wicket is not a very easy one to bat and their bowling lineup can turn things around pretty well.

The mid-overs phase went England's way as they conceded only 28 runs while picking up 4 crucial wickets in the phase of 7-15 overs. The boundaries dried up completely and runs came at a premium. Prisha Thanawala then went for the kill picking a couple more as the death overs approached and Tilly-Corteen Coleman too, made life difficult for the lower middle order and rushed through with a spectacular four-fer. Katie Jones showed her wicket-keeping skills masterfully and stumped out five Kiwi batters.

A timely break proved to be the turning point as England's bowlers returned with renewed vigor and tactical adjustments. Their smart variations in pace and length forced the Kiwi batters to take risks, sparking a dramatic collapse. New Zealand's promising start of 49 without loss crumbled into a concerning 68 for 4, as the wheels came off their innings. The English comeback was engineered by the bowling combination of Trudy Johnson, Phoebe Brett, and Prisha Thanawala. Working in tandem, they strung a streak of dot balls and got rewarded with crucial wickets in the middle overs.

England's pacers got that movement in the overcast morning conditions, and their spinners occasionally got some bit off the deck, but the breakthrough proved elusive. While the fielding didn't rise to the occasion, the New Zealand openers showed good intent, particularly feasting on anything that strayed wide of the off stump. England chopped and changed in the bowling in order to unsettle this Kiwi opening pair, and it was Trudy Johnson, the sixth bowler who provided the breakthrough. Irwin though, provided that solid platform for the others to build upon.

New Zealand Women stormed out of the blocks, with Kate Irwin leading the charge with intent. The damp outfield played its tricks, turning boundaries into hustled twos, but that hardly dampened the Kiwi spirits. Irwin, who was gifted an early life, made England pay as she and her partner, Emma McLeod crafted an unblemished powerplay score of 33.

This was quite a collapse for New Zealand Women Under-19 after the halfway mark. If we look at the scorecard, barring Kate Irwin and Emma McLeod, the openers, none of the Kiwi batters could cross the double figures and just kept following each other in a procession. A job well done by England bowlers and they would surely be the happier of the two sides with momentum, by restricting New Zealand below 100.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! New Zealand Women Under-19 are in a strong position as Kate Irwin and Emma McLeod provided a strong stand before the former perished. It is on the batters to come to build upon this momentum nicely along and bat through till the end. For England, they have been a bit sloppy in the field and the bowlers too, haven't quite bowled the tight lines and lengths. However, the wicket of Irwin could well serve as an opening for them. They would like to slow things a bit and snag a quick few more wickets to get back into the game. With 9 wickets in hand, the Kiwis surely must be eyeing a score around or above 120. But for that, they need to build meaningful partnerships. An exciting next half of the play on cards, folks!

Commentary.Commentary: UPDATE - 3.10 am GMT - Good news, folks! The rain has stopped now and the covers have come off as well. As expected, this was just a passing shower. Just a 10-minute delay, hence we won't be losing any overs as well. The umpires and players come out to the middle to continue the proceedings.

UPDATE - 3.00 am GMT - Uh, oh! It has started to rain out there and the umpires have called the players off the field. The covers are coming on and the pitch is being covered along with the squares. It looks like a passing shower as the rain has eased up a bit, and has been reduced into a mizzle now. So, hopefully, this won't be a long delay. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The players and the umpires walk out and take the field to start the match's first innings. England Women Under-19 have asked New Zealand Women Under-19 to have a bat first under the clouds. It is the pair of Emma McLeod and Kate Irwin walking out to bat for New Zealand Women Under-19. Well then, the players and the umpires walk out in straight lines and stand on the ground for the respective national anthems. It is the national anthem of New Zealand first, followed by that of England.

The captain of New Zealand Women Under-19, Tash Wakelin says that they would have batted first. Says that they have played a few games here. Also mentions that they have got a good set of batters in the side, and expects them to step up in this game and bat longer. Informs one change in the side.

The captain of England Women Under-19, Abigale Norgrove mentions the weather as the reason they want to use the overcast conditions early in the game. She further adds that it has been difficult for them to stick to one playing eleven because of the difference in the conditions. She ends by saying that they have made quite a few changes to the side for today.

New Zealand Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Emma McLeod, Kate Irwin, Anika Todd, Eve Wolland, Tash Wakelin (C), Darcy Prasad (WK), Rishika Jaswal, Louisa Kotkamp, Sophie Court, Ayaan Lambat (In for Anika Tauwhare), Hannah Francis.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in the favor of England Women Under-19 and they have opted to BOWL first.

Out of four spots, India, South Africa, and Australia have already punched their tickets for the semifinals, which leaves just one more to be filled. Both groups are tightly contested with at least five teams fighting for that one remaining spot. For New Zealand, as they stand in the fifth position of Group 2, this match is just like a virtual knockout for them. Meaning, a defeat and their chances will be dashed out. On the flip side, England holds a commanding second position in the same group just behind South Africa, but would like to keep on winning. It’s turning out to be a contest to watch out for with the semifinal berth on the line. Do stick around as the toss and team updates will flash shortly!

Cricket is all about setbacks and comebacks. This is exactly what has replicated in New Zealand’s journey so far. Facing two defeats in the group stage, their game against USA also went down to the wire. Their bowlers saved the day for them on the back of top-drawer performances from Kate Irwin and Rishika Jaswal. While the others too chipped in handy. However, as promising their batting unit looks on paper, they would be keen on to replicate the same when they come out to bat. Eve Wolland, Hannah Francis have displayed individual brilliance, but it’s time for the top order to step up and provide those strong foundations.

Weather has played its fair share in this tournament as well. With two matches washed out due to inclement weather England is one team that hasn’t been in much action. Their previous game was a complete washout against Nigeria, but they still have two commanding wins to show. In whatever cricket they have played so far, the girls from England have shown promise. Davina Perrin and Trudy Johnson have been their top scorers while Johnson has also delivered with the ball, as a complete all-rounder. Tilly Corteen-Coleman looked impressive with her bowling stints as well. With players stepping up when needed, this English side packs a serious punch.

Hello, everyone! Welcome to our coverage of the Super Six stage of the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025. Games come thick and fast in this competition and today we have two powerpacked teams, with a rich cricketing history and heritage on their backs. It’s England taking on New Zealand in Match number 7.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Super Six stage of the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup is heating up, and it’s been nothing short of thrilling, with every team bringing their A-game. While weather has played spoilsport for some, including England, whose first Super Six match against Nigeria was washed out, the action is far from slowing down. Up next, England’s young stars face off against New Zealand Under-19 at the Borneo Cricket Ground in Kuching. England’s journey so far has been a mix of highs and hurdles – they bowled Pakistan out for just 64 but also faced a tough challenge when they gave up over 100 runs to the USA. However, their ability to rise to the occasion and secure wins when it matters most has been a major boost for them, and they’ll be eager to carry that momentum forward. Davina Perrin has been a standout performer, leading the run charts of the tournament and becoming the only player to surpass the 100-run mark. Her consistency with the bat has been a huge asset, and she's had solid support from her teammates at crucial moments. England’s bowling attack has also held its ground, with Tilly Corteen-Coleman, who’s already featured in The Hundred Women’s Competition, stepping up with key contributions. However, as the tournament intensifies, the challenges are set to rise for England, and every team still in the mix. The stakes are higher, and the competition is only going to get tougher. When it comes to a never-say-die attitude, the White Ferns, or New Zealand Women Under-19, proved exactly why you can't count them out until the final ball. Facing intense pressure against the USA, they looked to be on the back foot, but pulled off an incredible heist in the end, thanks to some brilliant bowling that turned the game on its head. It was a true display of resilience and determination. Despite their thrilling win, the Kiwis know there's work to be done, particularly with their batting. The key challenge for them will be to avoid the dreaded collapses and shift their focus to building solid partnerships in the middle overs. If they can steady their batting line-up, they’ll be a much more formidable force as the competition heats up. New Zealand is fortunate to have promising players like skipper Tash Wakelin and Hannah Francis to anchor the middle order, but for that to be effective, the openers must lay a solid foundation upfront. With the stakes so high, a loss in this match could severely impact both teams' chances of advancing to the next stage, making this clash a crucial one for both sides. As the two cricketing powerhouses await to clash, fans can expect a real belter of a contest!
